text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Syrian President Hafez al-Assad sends messages to King Hassan of Morocco and Mauritanian President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya on latest developments of peace with Israel.
- Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez says Assad's role in the peace process is a decisive factor in the confrontation with Israel.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak will not deliver message from Assad to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
- Jordanian parties submit a memorandum to the Arab League demanding support for Syria in confrontation with "the Zionist campaign" and decide to hold a mass rally in solidarity with Syria on Feb 15.
- Israel accuses five Syrians in the Golan of carrying out resistance operations.
- The Higher Investment Council discusses industrial and agricultural projects, mainly in the textile and cereal processing sectors.
- Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs plans to import 222,000 tonnes of raw and white sugar in 1997 worth around $84 million.
- Egypt stresses that peace talks should resume on the basis that the Golan Heights should be returned to Syria.
- Russia tells the Arab League that it stands against Israeli settlements in the occupied Arab lands.
- New Israeli threats to south Lebanon.
